plotEn:
James Bowen is a destitute and homeless recovering heroin addict living on the streets of London. After a life-threatening drug-related incident, his support worker Val gets him off the street and into a council flat with a methadone prescription. On his first night in his flat James discovers a cat rifling through his food. James tries to return the cat to his owners, and lets him go. The cat returns to James's flat with a purulent wound on his back leg. James' animal-loving but allergic neighbour Betty directs James to a charity vet where she volunteers, and names the cat Bob. 
James misses a meeting with Val while waiting on a queue at the vet. James has Bob neutered and sets him free but Bob keeps following James into town. When Bob begins drawing crowds of people, and making James more panhandling money, he decides to keep Bob. Bob becomes a tourist hotspot and James and Betty become romantically attached.
James finds his old friend, Baz, unconscious on his flat estate, overdosed on heroin. Baz dies in hospital, and James finds out Betty can't be around drug addicts, as her deceased brother had been one. On New Year's Eve, James takes Bob to visit his biological father, Jack, his stepmother, Hilary, and his sisters, Pris and Faith. Bob destroys their living room, and Hilary sends James and Bob out.
During a busking performance, James argues with a thug and James is arrested for the ensuing crowd brawl. He's cleared of charges but prohibited from busking for six months. H
